title.es: Redactar el resumen de un segmento

es: Escribir un resumen fiel de un segmento de audio con tres verbos de habla, según + hablante y la postura de cada participante.

teaching.en: A faithful summary keeps the main points, attributes every idea to its speaker and never adds an opinion of your own.
teaching.es: Un resumen fiel conserva los puntos principales, atribuye cada idea a su hablante y nunca añade una opinión propia.
teaching.explanationEs: Faithful = fiel: no cambias lo que dijo cada persona ni añades juicios tuyos.
segments: A faithful summary keeps the main points, attributes every idea to
its speaker and never adds an opinion of your own.
teaching.audioText: A faithful summary keeps the main points, attributes every idea to its speaker and never adds an opinion of your own.

teaching.en: According to the guest, recordings are valuable study tools, whereas the host is more cautious about what they might cost.
teaching.es: Según la invitada, las grabaciones son herramientas de estudio valiosas, mientras que el presentador es más cauteloso sobre lo que podrían costar.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + hablante atribuye la idea; whereas contrasta dos posturas en la misma frase.
segments: According to the guest, recordings are valuable study tools, whereas
the host is more cautious about what they might cost.
teaching.audioText: According to the guest, recordings are valuable study tools, whereas the host is more cautious about what they might cost.

teaching.en: The guest sounds confident because she is ready to advocate recording every lesson, and she is quick to dismiss the worry that it empties the classroom.
teaching.es: La invitada suena segura porque está dispuesta a defender la grabación de todas las clases y es rápida en restar valor al temor de que vacíe el aula.
teaching.explanationEs: Advocate + -ing defiende una propuesta; dismiss resta valor a una objeción. Sounds + adjetivo describe la postura.
segments: The guest sounds confident because she is ready to advocate recording every lesson,
and she is quick to dismiss the worry that it empties the classroom.
teaching.audioText: The guest sounds confident because she is ready to advocate recording every lesson, and she is quick to dismiss the worry that it empties the classroom.

teaching.en: The host is sceptical: he wants to raise a concern about the cost, but he does not reject the idea completely.
teaching.es: El presentador es escéptico: quiere plantear una preocupación sobre el coste, pero no rechaza la idea por completo.
teaching.explanationEs: Raise a concern = plantear una preocupación; sceptical describe una postura de duda.
segments: The host is sceptical: he wants to raise a concern about
the cost, but he does not reject the idea completely.
teaching.audioText: The host is sceptical: he wants to raise a concern about the cost, but he does not reject the idea completely.

teaching.en: A good summary can highlight the stance of each speaker with verbs such as claim, admit or warn instead of repeating says.
teaching.es: Un buen resumen puede destacar la postura de cada hablante con verbos como claim, admit o warn en lugar de repetir says.
teaching.explanationEs: Stance = postura; highlight la destaca con verbos de habla variados.
segments: A good summary can highlight the stance of each speaker with
verbs such as claim, admit or warn instead of repeating says.

teaching.en: Overall, the segment shows that both speakers want the same result, even if they disagree about how to reach it.
teaching.es: En conjunto, el segmento muestra que ambos hablantes quieren el mismo resultado, aunque discrepen sobre cómo lograrlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Overall cierra el resumen con una valoración global; se escribe al final y con coma.

prompt.es: Elige la frase de resumen que atribuye con fidelidad las ideas del fragmento.

choices.text: According to the host, phones are useful only for specific tasks, whereas the guest prefers a full ban.
According to the guest, phones should be banned, whereas the host sounds confident about them.
According to the guest, phones are useful only for specific tasks, whereas the host prefers a full ban.

feedback.es: La invitada defiende un uso limitado y el presentador prefiere prohibirlos: las otras frases intercambian a los hablantes o deforman sus ideas.

hint.es: Comprueba quién dice cada idea antes de fijarte en el conector.

origin.text: Guest: Phones are useful tools, but only when a task really needs them. Host: I am not convinced; a full ban would be simpler to control.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quiere plantear una preocupación sobre el tiempo de pantalla antes del cierre.»

feedback.es: Raise a concern es la colocación habitual para plantear una preocupación; el contraste con la invitada marca su postura.

hint.es: El verbo va con «a concern» y significa plantear o sacar un tema.

origin.text: The guest sounds relaxed about the new rule. The host, in contrast, wants to ___ a concern about screen time before the segment ends.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura de la presentadora refleja mejor este fragmento?

choices.text: She is cautiously positive after some early doubts.
She was enthusiastic about it from the very first day.
She is sceptical and advises listeners to avoid it.

feedback.es: Admite que al principio le costó, pero ahora está convencida: su postura es positiva, aunque con dudas iniciales.

origin.text: The presenter says she has used the app for a month. She admits that it took a while to get used to, but she is now convinced and tells listeners to give it a chance.

prompt.es: Resume con un verbo de habla lo que dice la invitada.

answer.text: The guest dismisses the idea that recordings make students lazy.
accepted: The guest dismisses the idea that recordings make students lazy.
According to the guest, recordings do not make students lazy.
The guest rejects the idea that recordings make students lazy.

feedback.es: Dismiss o reject expresan que rechaza una idea; el resumen atribuye la postura a la invitada sin copiar su frase.

origin.text: Guest: «I reject the idea that recordings make students lazy. In my experience, they review more, not less.»

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige la postura de la colega al final.

choices.text: She has been fully convinced by the director's case.
She stays doubtful but agrees to a limited trial.
She supports the plan only if clients are told in advance.

feedback.es: Sigue sin convencerse («still doubtful»), pero acepta una prueba de tres meses: duda y cede de forma limitada.

origin.audio: In a staff meeting, the director presents a plan to move to a four-day week. She sounds confident and claims that results will improve, pointing to a trial in another city. Her colleague raises a concern: clients may feel ignored on Fridays. The director acknowledges this and suggests keeping one person in the office. The colleague is still doubtful, but she agrees to support a three-month trial. Overall, the meeting ends with a cautious agreement.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué fin menciona la directora una prueba en otra ciudad.

choices.text: To answer the concern about clients on Fridays.
To show that other companies have copied her plan.
To give evidence for her claim that results will improve.

feedback.es: La prueba en otra ciudad respalda su afirmación de que los resultados mejorarán; no responde a la objeción de los clientes.

prompt.es: Escribe el resumen del segmento: tres verbos de habla y la postura de cada hablante.

answer.text: In this segment, the host and Dr Patel debate whether schools should record every lesson. Dr Patel is in favour: she maintains that recordings help students who miss a class or need to watch a difficult explanation again. She acknowledges that attendance may fall, but she insists that learning matters more than attendance. The host, by contrast, is sceptical. He fears that students will stop coming to school, and he points out that teachers feel watched. Dr Patel accepts that this is a fair concern, so she suggests recording only the main lessons and letting teachers remove private comments. The host calls this a reasonable compromise. Overall, the guest sounds confident, whereas the host remains cautious, but both want to protect learning.
accepted: In this segment, the host and Dr Patel debate whether schools should record every lesson. Dr Patel is in favour: she maintains that recordings help students who miss a class or need to watch a difficult explanation again. She acknowledges that attendance may fall, but she insists that learning matters more than attendance. The host, by contrast, is sceptical. He fears that students will stop coming to school, and he points out that teachers feel watched. Dr Patel accepts that this is a fair concern, so she suggests recording only the main lessons and letting teachers remove private comments. The host calls this a reasonable compromise. Overall, the guest sounds confident, whereas the host remains cautious, but both want to protect learning.

The segment is a debate between a host and Dr Patel about whether schools should record every lesson. According to the guest, recordings are useful for students who miss a class, and she argues that learning is more important than attendance. She admits that attendance could fall and accepts that teachers may feel watched, so she proposes recording only the main lessons. The host is sceptical because he worries that students will stop coming to school. He claims that a fully online model is risky, but he still calls her idea a reasonable compromise. To sum up, the guest is confident and practical, whereas the host is more cautious, although both speakers care about good learning.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen presenta el tema, atribuye las ideas con verbos variados, marca la postura de cada uno y cierra con una valoración global.

origin.text:
Host: Today we ask whether schools should record every lesson. Dr Patel, you are in favour.
Guest: I am. Recordings help students who miss a class, and they can watch a difficult explanation again. I acknowledge that attendance may fall, but I maintain that learning matters more than attendance.
Host: I am sceptical. If everything is online, will students still come? Also, teachers say they feel watched.
Guest: That is a fair concern, which is why I suggest recording only the main lessons and letting teachers remove private comments.
Host: That is a reasonable compromise. Before we go, thank you, Dr Patel.

prompt.es: Lee el correo de la oyente. ¿Qué actitud transmite hacia la invitada?

choices.text: Mostly positive, with one question left unanswered.
Completely negative about the whole argument.
Not interested, because the segment said very little.

feedback.es: Valora el argumento («I liked») y deja pendiente un punto concreto (quién pagaría el equipo): aprobación con una duda.

origin.text: Listener's email: Thank you for the segment on recording lessons. I liked the guest's argument, although she never explained who would pay for the equipment. I hope you come back to that point next week.

feedback.es: Overall va al principio, con coma, y resume la valoración global del segmento.
